index.meta.description: European projects and partnerships at Ippeios Primary School, Lesvos, Greece.
index.text.018: From Ippeios on the island of Lesvos, our school opens its doors to Europe and creates new opportunities for learning, cooperation and creativity. Through Erasmus+ and eTwinning, pupils and teachers discover different cultures, exchange ideas, share experiences and explore new approaches to learning.
index.text.019: Every European partnership gives us a chance to see the world from a different perspective, develop new skills and enrich our daily school life. For us,
index.text.020: going beyond borders means broadening the opportunities available to every child.
index.text.029: School year 2026–2027 · Different partnerships, shared educational aims.
index.text.030: Our approved KA122 project “Sustainable Tourism Starts at School” and our participation in the KA121 consortium coordinated by Skopelos Primary School.
index.text.032: Two European collaborative projects: “Sustainable Tourism Starts at School” and “Next-Gen Learning in Future-Ready Schools”.
index.text.036: Our school has a long record of European cooperation: eTwinning projects recognised with National and European Quality Labels, two eTwinning School awards (2023–2024 and 2025–2026), the Jean Monnet GenEUs project, and Erasmus+ partnerships and mobilities.

index.text.065: Through our Erasmus+ KA122 project “Sustainable Tourism Starts at School”, we explore how caring for our home can become a shared learning experience.

school.meta.title: Our school | Ippeios Primary School
school.meta.description: European projects and partnerships at Ippeios Primary School, Lesvos, Greece.
school.text.014: In the heart of rural Lesvos, our school grows through the ideas and experiences of its pupils.
school.text.015: Every child has something to contribute
school.text.016: Our school community brings together different stories, languages and backgrounds. We make room for collaboration and hands-on learning: observing, discussing, trying ideas and learning from one another.
school.text.018: Olive groves, villages, local routes, people and the Petrified Forest of Lesvos inspire important questions: how can we protect what we love and share our home with respect?

erasmus.meta.title: Erasmus+ | Ippeios Primary School
erasmus.meta.description: European projects and partnerships at Ippeios Primary School, Lesvos, Greece.
erasmus.text.014: This school year, we are taking part in two distinct Erasmus+ actions, both focused on bringing new learning back into our classrooms.
erasmus.text.016: Our approved project begins with a question that matters to us: how can we welcome visitors while protecting the places we love? Through mobility, training and joint activities, we aim to strengthen sustainable experiential learning, inclusion and digital collaboration across our school.
erasmus.text.020: We are part of a five-school consortium sharing educational experiences and mobility opportunities. Our KA121 consortium participation is separate from our own KA122 project and our eTwinning partnerships.
erasmus.text.024: Agiasos Primary School, Palaiokipos Primary School, 10th Primary School of Mytilene and Ippeios Primary School.

etwinning.text.014: Two opportunities for collaboration, through shared activities, ideas and creations travelling from classroom to classroom.
etwinning.text.016: Pupils become responsible visitors and storytellers of their own place. They explore nature, cultural heritage and how to make destinations welcoming and sustainable.
etwinning.text.017: We begin with Mystery Classroom and a pupil logo competition. Our shared missions then focus on responsible visiting, cultural heritage and European hospitality.
etwinning.text.018: Our international collaboration takes place in TwinSpace. Here we share selected outcomes and moments that can be made public.
etwinning.text.020: Through “Next-Gen Learning in Future-Ready Schools”, we explore new ways to learn, create and work together. The project connects schools participating in the KA121 consortium coordinated by Skopelos Primary School.
etwinning.text.021: The project poster introduces our shared vision of tomorrow's school.

results.meta.title: Results and deliverables | Ippeios Primary School
results.meta.description: European projects and partnerships at Ippeios Primary School, Lesvos, Greece.
results.text.014: Here we present the commitments of our approved KA122 project: how we aim to improve teaching, what pupils will create and how progress will be assessed.
results.text.015: Planned targets — not results already achieved.
results.text.016: These commitments come from the approved KA122 application and our internal monitoring framework. Some items describe implementation and evidence practices rather than separate deliverables submitted to the EU.
results.text.020: By the end of the project, at least 70% of teachers should regularly integrate sustainability or experiential environmental learning into their teaching (baseline: below 30%).
results.text.023: At least 80% of pupils with fewer opportunities should contribute to a collaborative product, and at least 70% should show improved participation and confidence compared with the baseline.
results.text.026: At least one organised digital collaboration and one sustainability-related digital product per class; use of 3–5 tools; at least 75% of pupils improving their collaborative digital skills.
results.text.028: The following sections describe planned commitments and supporting evidence. They will be updated with actual results as the project progresses.
results.text.031: By the end of the project, at least 70% of teachers should regularly integrate sustainability or experiential environmental learning into their teaching (baseline: below 30%).
results.text.033: Two interdisciplinary sustainability projects per school year and at least six shared lesson plans, supported by implementation evidence.
results.text.035: At least 80% of pupils with fewer opportunities should contribute to a collaborative product, and at least 70% should show improved participation and confidence compared with the baseline.
results.text.037: At least one organised digital collaboration and one sustainability-related digital product per class; use of 3–5 tools; at least 75% of pupils improving their collaborative digital skills.
results.text.039: A shared physical and digital space for collecting, accessing and reusing teaching materials, lesson plans and pupil creations.
results.text.040: A practical resource pack with lesson-plan templates, green and experiential activities, inclusion strategies, digital tasks and observation tools.
results.text.042: Recording, testing, adapting and reusing practices gained through job shadowing and professional development.
results.text.043: A permanent Erasmus+ corner and digital knowledge hub giving access to outputs, examples and school-community updates.
results.text.045: Two formal staff reviews per school year, monitoring every two months by the Erasmus+ team, and an annual review with the school education advisor.
results.text.047: A shared responsible tourism guide featuring pupil observations and materials from mobilities and cooperation with host schools.
results.text.049: At least one joint sustainability-related product developed with host-school pupils, through blended and face-to-face cooperation and continued collaboration after returning home.
results.text.051: Eco-guides, posters, presentations, field observations, digital products and cross-curricular work connected to our local area.
results.text.053: Strengthening cooperation, democratic participation, respect for diversity and responsible care for cultural and natural heritage.
results.text.056: Learning goals, getting to know the host school, digital buddies, language and cultural preparation, safety measures and support.
results.text.058: Guided visits, observation sheets, simple digital recording, collaborative activities and daily reflection.
results.text.060: Pre- and post-mobility reflections, a four-level participation rubric and self-assessment; target: at least 80% recognising sustainable and unsustainable tourism practices.
results.text.062: Transparent selection criteria, 40% of pupil places reserved for those with fewer opportunities, and support before, during and after mobility.
results.text.065: Reflective journals, observation sheets, pilot lessons, in-school workshops, peer observation and mentoring.
results.text.066: An internal evidence collection including comparable baseline/final assessments, reflections, lesson plans and products, without publishing personal data.
results.text.068: Staff workshops, pupil presentations, parent updates, local activities, a regional event and selected results shared on eTwinning and the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform.
results.text.070: Sustaining the work after the project
results.text.071: Integrating experiential and environmental learning into the school's annual development plan, mentoring new teachers and maintaining European partnerships.
results.text.073: Documented recognition of learning outcomes, official acknowledgement of EU support in project materials and public updates through the Erasmus+ corner.
